chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from the Virtuous Slave (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'What is the waiting period (iddah) of a young woman who menstruates like others, whose husband divorces her, and then her menstruation ceases?' He said, 'Three months.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, for she married after three months, and it became clear to her after entering to her husband that she was pregnant.' He said, 'Far from that, O Ibn Hakim. The cessation of menstruation is of two types: either it is the corruption (cessation) of a period of menstruation, so she is permitted to marry and is not pregnant; or she is pregnant, and this becomes clear within three months, because Allah, the Exalted, has made it a time in which the pregnancy becomes clear.'

I said to him, 'But what if she is in doubt (uncertain if pregnant or not)?' He said, 'Her waiting period is nine months.' I said, 'But what if she is in doubt after nine months?' He said, 'Pregnancy is only nine months.' I said, 'Then she marries?' He said, 'She exercises caution (waits) for three months.' I said, 'But what if she is in doubt after three months?' He said, 'There is no more doubt upon her; she may marry.'

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period (Iddah) for a divorced or widowed woman

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a woman whose menstruation stops unexpectedly after divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the *Iddah* (waiting period) for a young woman experiencing *Istihaza* or cessation of menstruation, distinguishing between natural cessation and pregnancy. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that while pregnancy is typically confirmed within three months, any lingering doubt after this period is resolved in favor of freedom to remarry, reflecting the Shia principle of removing hardship (*Raf' al-Haraj*). This ruling underscores the jurisprudential balance between certainty and permissible doubt in personal status law.
